//prose: 2.1.0: `name` is dropped into carrier sentences ("One useful alert for X is ___"), so it must be a NOUN PHRASE in the recipient's second person. Fixed here: an imperative ("Claim newly funded accounts first"), a UI label ("API / data feed"), and a third-person reference to the reader ("the broker's market").
//: Use-case catalog per SPEC-v2 §3 (USE-001..004): selection returns ONLY entries from this file, primary first, max three, deterministic per ICP. example_alert strings must describe alerts Fundable can actually express — every one below is built from filters verified against the live API (industries, locations, stage/round, employee count, date windows, hiring-plan mentions in deal descriptions). 'Companies expanding into a new geo' has NO structured signal; where the spec's table implies it, the example uses the honest proxy (funded + territory/new-market phrasing from deal text).

1.name: Funded companies signaling hiring
1.why_relevant: A fresh raise plus stated hiring plans means they need talent before they have recruiters.
1.example_alert: US startups that raised seed-Series B in the last 7 days and mention growing the team.

1.name: Raises filtered to your sector and stage
1.why_relevant: Reach them before other talent shops do.
1.example_alert: AI startups that raised in the last 24 hours, 11-100 employees.

2.name: Recently funded companies in your market
2.why_relevant: A recent raise can precede office expansion.
2.example_alert: Bay Area startups that raised in the past 24 hours.

2.name: Territory watch by stage
2.why_relevant: Series B+ raises are the strongest space-demand signal.
2.example_alert: NY companies that raised Series B or later this week.

4.name: Newly funded startups, daily
4.why_relevant: Deposits move right after a round closes.
4.example_alert: A daily digest of every startup that raised in your segment.

4.name: Territory alerts with founder contacts
4.why_relevant: First call after the wire lands wins the account.
4.example_alert: SF fintech raises this week, with founder contact info.

5.name: First claim on newly funded accounts
5.why_relevant: Post-raise companies get budget; first rep to claim owns the account.
5.example_alert: Companies in your ICP that raised in the last hour.

5.name: Stealth and first-raise emergence
5.example_alert: Companies emerging from stealth with their first announced round.

6.name: Investors active in your space
6.why_relevant: See who is actually writing cheques at your stage before you raise.
6.example_alert: Funds that led seed rounds in your sector in the last 90 days.

6.name: Deal history and round research
6.why_relevant: Know a fund's real activity before the first call.
6.example_alert: Every round a target fund participated in, with dates and co-investors.

7.name: Investor lists matched to each client
7.why_relevant: Ground every intro list in live deal activity rather than a stale database.
7.example_alert: Active seed investors in climate for a client raising now.

8.name: Thesis monitoring
8.why_relevant: See every company crossing into your thesis the day it happens.
8.example_alert: B2B SaaS companies raising Series B+ at $20M+ rounds.

8.name: Repeat-founder signals
8.why_relevant: Second-time founders raise faster; be earliest.
8.example_alert: New rounds where the company's founders previously built a funded startup.

9.name: API and data-feed access
9.why_relevant: Build on live funding, investor, and people data instead of scraping.
9.example_alert: REST access to rounds, investors, and people as they are tracked.

9.name: MCP inside Claude/ChatGPT
9.why_relevant: Query the dataset from the tools your team already uses.
9.example_alert: Fundable MCP connected to your assistant for company research.

10.name: Companies entering new geographies
10.why_relevant: Funded companies moving into a new market need cross-border payments and FX support.
10.example_alert: Funded startups whose round announcements mention international or new-market expansion.

10.name: Funded international startups
10.why_relevant: A raise outside your home market is a cross-border moment by definition.
10.example_alert: European startups raising US rounds this month.

11.name: Hiring and headcount signals with HR buyers
11.why_relevant: Post-raise headcount growth is when payroll and PEO decisions get made.
11.example_alert: Raises this week that mention hiring plans, with People/HR contacts.

11.name: New-geography signals
11.why_relevant: A company hiring in a new country needs an employer of record fast.
11.example_alert: Funded startups whose announcements mention expanding the team internationally.

12.name: Post-raise buying moments
12.why_relevant: D&O and cyber get bought right after the round closes.
12.example_alert: Series A+ raises this week with finance and operations contacts.

13.name: Funded startups moving upmarket
13.why_relevant: Compliance gets bought when a funded startup starts selling to bigger customers.
13.example_alert: B2B startups that raised Series A/B in the last 30 days.

14.name: Fresh raises with hiring plans
14.why_relevant: Reach them the week the hiring budget appears.
14.example_alert: Raises in the last 7 days mentioning team growth, with recruiting contacts.

15.name: Post-raise finance needs
15.why_relevant: New money means audits, bookkeeping, and a finance stack decision.
15.example_alert: Seed and Series A raises this week, with founder contacts.

16.name: Newly funded companies ready to spend
16.why_relevant: Describe your ICP once; get pinged when a matching company raises and has budget.
16.example_alert: US companies Series B+ that raised in the last 24 hours.

17.name: Post-raise legal needs
17.why_relevant: Rounds create financing docs, new entities, and hiring paperwork.
17.example_alert: First-time raises this month, with founder contacts.

18.name: Raise and launch signals with marketing contacts
18.why_relevant: Announcement week is when startups buy marketing and PR help.
18.example_alert: Seed-Series A raises this week in consumer, with marketing contacts.

19.name: Thesis-based deal alerts
19.why_relevant: See every round in your thesis the day it is announced, not in next month's newsletter.

19.name: Portfolio and milestone monitoring
19.why_relevant: Know when a portfolio or watchlist company raises, before it is news.
19.example_alert: Any new round for the 40 companies on your watchlist.

20.name: Funded accounts matching your exact ICP
20.why_relevant: Describe your ICP in natural language; get pinged when a matching company raises.
20.example_alert: Your ICP description, evaluated against every new round hourly.

20.name: Enriched buyer contacts
20.why_relevant: Rounds arrive with the people you would actually reach out to.
20.example_alert: New raises in your segment with verified buyer contact info.
